name: Planning Center
description: Service planning, volunteer schedules, check-in, giving, and the people list, for churches. Eleven products. Two church staffers started it in 2006 to replace their own Sunday spreadsheet. Carlsbad. Founder-owned, no funding, debt-free, no sales team, and locked as not for sale through a foundation.

mentions.evidence: The company says 78,000 active churches, 4 million active users, 200 or more employees, and more than $34 billion in donations processed. It does not publish revenue. Those donations are money that passed through the giving tool, not Planning Center's own revenue. RocketReach estimates about $19.4 million a year in 2026. That is a rough guess next to a staff of 200 or more.
mentions.indieAngle: One Sunday job, done plainly. The bulletin, the translation, the kids' check-in. It can move from one church to the next without a sales team.

whyItPrints: Sunday happens every week. The same volunteers, the same check-in, the same giving. A church tells the next church.
whyThisMatters: Sunday is a weekly operation. Who is singing, who is in the nursery, who checked in, and what landed in the plate. Planning Center is eleven products for that week: the service plan, the volunteers, check-in, giving, and the people list. Two people on a church staff started it in 2006, in Carlsbad, because their spreadsheet was the system. It is still founder-owned. They did not take funding, they say they are debt-free, they have no sales team, and a foundation locks it as not for sale. The about page says seventy-eight thousand active churches, four million active users, and two hundred or more employees. It also says more than thirty-four billion has been processed as donations. That money belonged to the churches. It is not Planning Center's revenue, and they do not publish a revenue number. RocketReach guesses about nineteen point four million a year for 2026. Next to a staff of two hundred, that guess is rough, and I am not promoting it to a company figure. One Sunday job, the bulletin or the kids' check-in, is enough of a product to move from one church to the next by word of mouth.
